title: Intra-Epidermal Fiber Density Determination in Rodent Foot Pad Biopsies
author: Eva Feldman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7rehm3e

steps.title: Harvest Foot Pad Tissue
steps.instruction: Remove the entire foot pad from a perfused mouse or rat using a sharp razor blade.

substeps.instruction: Cut skin between the plantar surface of the foot and the toes.
Start at the heel to gently remove the skin and superficial fascia of the foot.
Handle the tissue only by the heel.

steps.title: Fix and Process Tissue
steps.instruction: Fix the harvested tissue and dehydrate using a sucrose gradient.

substeps.instruction: Post-fix the tissue overnight in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Rinse in graded sucrose (5% to 20%), remaining in each concentration for a minimum of 12 hours.

steps.title: Process Fresh Tissue
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh mouse or rat foot samples for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Remove the foot and fix overnight (12-18 hours) in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Remove the skin and process as described in the perfused tissue steps.

steps.title: Perform Immunohistochemistry
steps.instruction: Stain the tissue for PGP9.5 fibers.

substeps.instruction: Apply rabbit anti-PGP9.5 at a 1:1000 dilution.
Apply AlexaFluor 598 at a 1:200 dilution (Molecular Probes).
Apply coverslips using the ProLong antifade kit (Molecular Probes).

steps.title: Image the Samples
steps.instruction: Collect confocal images of the samples using an Olympus FluoView 500 microscope.

substeps.instruction: Use a 60 X 1.2 water immersion objective.
Set optical section thickness to 0.5 um.

steps.title: Analyze Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Process and analyze the collected image stacks.

substeps.instruction: Flatten forty images per stack using the MetaMorph (version 6.14) arithmetic option.
Use integrated morphometry analysis to exclude extraneous signals.
Calculate the percent area of PGP9.5 positive fibers per area of epidermis.
